title: I. The Mandate
text:
You are B.J. Habibie, 3rd President of the Republic of Indonesia. Following the June 1999 legislative elections, you have four months to govern the country before the 700 delegates of the People's Consultative Assembly (MPR) convene in Senayan on October 19, 1999.

Under the 1945 Constitution, the MPR—not the popular vote—decides the fate of your presidency. To survive and secure a full term, you must win a majority of at least 351 votes to accept your Accountability Speech (Pidato Pertanggungjawaban).

There are no raw numbers on your dashboard. You must rely on qualitative intelligence, press reactions, and the shifting moods of the Assembly.

title: II. National Metrics
text:
Your administration is tracked across seven metrics on the left panel:

• Popularity: Public sentiment. High popularity warms MPR delegates each turn; low popularity erodes their trust.
• Military Support: Your standing with Cilangkap, tied directly to the ABRI parliamentary bloc.
• Reformasi Credibility: Trust among students, the press, and democratic reformers. Letting it collapse triggers street unrest.
• Economic Health: The strength of the rupiah and staple prices. Economic freefall damages both Popularity and Stability.
• International Standing: Credibility with foreign capitals and the IMF. Low standing triggers capital flight that hurts the economy.
• National Stability: Civic order. When stability drops, unrest inflates the Political Capital cost of all decrees and negotiations.
• Cendana Influence: The entrenched power of Suharto's inner circle. High Cendana Influence is harmful—it drains your Political Capital each turn, erodes Reformasi Credibility, and sabotages wavering delegates during the final vote.

Together, these metrics determine your GOVERNMENT STABILITY. A STABLE or SECURE government yields passive Political Capital each turn, while an UNSTABLE government suffers compounding fatigue.

title: III. The Action Phase
text:
Each turn begins with a historical Crisis Event, followed by the Political Action Phase. During each Action Phase, you have the bandwidth to take two actions:

1. One Executive Directive:
• Routine Executive Actions cost nothing and generate Political Capital (PC) while shifting national metrics. Repeating the exact same directive yields diminishing returns, and each action has a brief cooldown.
• Extraordinary Decrees expend Political Capital to pass major laws that permanently lock metric floors or cap Cendana Influence.

2. One Parliamentary Engagement:
• Select any faction in the MPR Dashboard below (via Faction View or Parliament View) to lobby, negotiate, or trade concessions once per turn.

title: IV. Factions, Leverage & Favors
text:
Each faction values specific national metrics. Maintaining high standings in a faction's preferred metrics gives you Strong or Absolute Bargaining Leverage, which reduces lobbying costs and boosts the goodwill gained:

• PDI-P & PKB: Value Popularity and Reformasi Credibility.
• Golkar (Akbar): Values Economic Health, Stability, and Cendana Influence.
• Golkar (Loyalists): Values Reformasi Credibility, Economic Health, and International Standing.
• PAN: Values Reformasi Credibility and Popularity.
• PPP & Other Parties: Value National Stability and Popularity.
• ABRI: Values Military Support and National Stability.
• Utusan Daerah: Values Economic Health and National Stability.
• Utusan Golongan: Values Reformasi Credibility and International Standing.

Political Favors:
Certain major concessions grant a Favor. Favors can be cashed in during the final turns using a faction's Final Appeal for a large loyalty surge, or held into Election Night to steady wavering delegates against last-minute defections.

title: V. The General Session
text:
Keep a close eye on these two two stats as October approaches:

• The Military Accommodation: General Wiranto begins in a pragmatic accommodation with the Palace that prevents ABRI support from dropping below a neutral floor. However, repeatedly crossing military red lines will strain and permanently break this pact.
• Voting Behavior: On October 19, disciplined command blocs (such as PDI-P and ABRI) vote heavily along their leadership's stance, whereas fragmented caucuses (Golkar, Utusan Daerah, Utusan Golongan, and Other Parties) split proportionally based on their goodwill, your Government Stability, and any Cendana interference behind the curtain.
